text:
sara: Quick heads-up — ran a per-model perf sweep (throughput & p95 latency) for Mixtral-8x7B and Qwen-14B on the staging infer cluster. Found a weird KV-cache eviction/merge pattern on Mixtral that correlates with a ~120ms/token latency bump once context > 4096.

alex: can you drop the trace + the kernel selection log?

sara: pasted below — it's the stack from the pprof sampler + our runtime kernel chooser log. noticed the runtime flips kernel variants mid-request when head_dim==96 and seq_len crosses 2048, which lines up with the jump.

sara: ```
pprof: top samples (sampled wall ns)
- attention_fast_v2: 42%
- aten_gemm_fallback: 31%
- kv_cache_merge: 12%
- other: 15%

runtime.log: kernel_select(model=Mixtral-8x7B, head_dim=96, seq_len=4096) -> select=aten_gemm_fallback (reason=quantized_kernel_mismatch)
runtime.log: kernel_select(seq_len=4097) -> select=attention_fast_v2 (reason=seq_len_over_threshold)
kv: evict triggered (current_kv_mem=1.38GB, thresh=1.2GB)
kv: merge cost ~9ms per row, observed ripple across following tokens
```

maria: hmm — that eviction thresh (1.2GB) is the default for the staging pool. Mixtral's KV representation is denser because we're storing per-head float16 chunks after the FFN rewrite. When eviction+merge happens in the middle of a long chat, we see a temporary serialization point while the merge completes, hence the per-token spike.

jon: any relation to RoPE scaling? We changed the RoPE scaling patch on Mixtral in the last rollout which also altered head kv stride layout. Could cause kernel mismatch.

sara: good catch — the RoPE patch changed per-head packing so quantized kernel signatures no longer matched our fast path. The kernel selector then falls back to aten_gemm for a bit, then back to fast_attn once it detects seq_len/packing alignment. That flip is expensive.

alex: actionable items?

maria: proposed fixes (short list):
- bump kv_eviction_threshold to 1.6GB for Mixtral pools (reduces mid-request evictions).
- teach kernel selector to prefer stable kernel variant across small sequence length transitions when the quantization signature mismatch is only packing-related (i.e., prefer fast_attn_v2 if head_dim and dtype match).
- add a tiny hysteresis window for seq_len boundary flips (e.g., if seq_len crosses threshold for < 200ms, don't reselect).
- microbatch cap: for Mixtral set microbatch_max=8 on A100s to avoid L2 thrashing we saw at microbatch 16+.

sara: also added a short-term mitigation in the staging config: kv_eviction_threshold=1.6GB + batcher.adaptive_prefix_preserve=true. Re-ran sweep and p95 improved ~18% for long contexts.

jon: what about Qwen-14B? Did you see similar behavior?

sara: Qwen behaved differently — its kernel selector picks the quantized GEMM path consistently because head_dim=128 and our quant kernels match. Throughput slightly better at batch sizes >=12. No mid-request evictions observed up to 8k context.

perf-bot: automated regression check: commit 0f3a7b2 introduced the RoPE packing change; perf delta: Mixtral-8x7B p95 +23% on long-context workload.

alex: ok. Plan: 1) revert or patch the RoPE packing change to retain compatible kernel signatures (short-term), 2) land kernel-selector hysteresis + preference rules (mid-term), 3) tune eviction thresholds per-model (config), 4) add a microbenchmark to catch cross-boundary kernel flips in CI. I'll file follow-ups. @eng-runtime please watch the canary we pushed to prod tomorrow. :eyes:

maria: filing the follow-ups now and adding the repro script to perf-regressions repo.

sara: thanks — I'll keep the staging sweep artifacts and add a runbook note: recommended config for Mixtral-8x7B on A100: `kv_eviction_threshold=1.6GB`, `microbatch_max=8`, kernel_preference=[fast_attn_v2, aten_gemm_fallback], `batcher.adaptive_prefix_preserve=true`.

jon: LGTM. If we need a hotfix, we can toggle the RoPE packing flag in the model adapter until kernel selector is safer.

alex: nice work, @sara and @maria. small PRs preferred, let's keep changes targeted. :thumbsup:

sara: saving logs to s3:/redwood/perf/sweeps/1769123456/ and adding links to the ticket.
